stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams via Acquisition of DoubleO.ai
stories.plain: ZoomInfo bought DoubleO.ai to launch Agent Teams — coordinated AI agents that run full go-to-market plays from signal to action without human babysitting. This matters because it moves agentic AI from a buzzword into a shipped GTM product backed by a major data vendor, raising the bar for how revenue teams buy and deploy AI agents at scale.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust™ to Add Continuous Intent Verification to Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: Experian and DataDome now jointly verify not just who an AI agent represents, but whether its actions stay within what it was authorized to do throughout a transaction. This is a concrete step toward governance infrastructure for agentic commerce — the kind of guardrail regulators and enterprise buyers will increasingly require before letting agents spend money autonomously.

stories.head: Contentstack Canoe Launches as Standalone AI Visibility Tool Showing Brands How AI Describes Them
stories.plain: Contentstack's first standalone product audits how a brand is named, described, and cited inside AI search engines, benchmarks it against up to ten rivals, and outputs a prioritized fix list that AI agents can act on. It is a rare commercial GEO product with a competitor benchmarking layer, making it directly relevant to budget decisions in search and content teams.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create 'AI Shelves' That Rewrite Brand and Price Competition
stories.plain: Jellyfish's research shows that AI shopping assistants surface product sets that look nothing like traditional search results, disrupting established brand hierarchies and price anchors. Paired with the launch of their Share of Model™ Shopping Optimization tool, this gives marketers concrete evidence — and a new buying category — for influencing what AI recommends at the point of purchase.

stories.head: Mixpanel Launches Agent Intelligence to Connect AI Agent Conversations to Business Outcomes
stories.plain: Mixpanel's new Agent Intelligence layer links what an AI agent says in conversation directly to downstream customer behavior and revenue metrics. This closes a major measurement gap: teams building or buying AI agents now have a path to proving ROI rather than guessing, which will shape how agentic AI is evaluated and governed inside product and marketing orgs.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams via DoubleO.ai Acquisition
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and used it to launch Agent Teams, a product that coordinates multiple AI agents across a company's GTM systems — from detecting a buying signal all the way to taking action — without human hand-holding at every step. This matters because it signals enterprise GTM vendors are moving from single-agent experiments to orchestrated multi-agent workflows.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust™ to Verify Agentic Commerce Continuously
stories.plain: Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem now uses DataDome to check not just who an AI agent is, but whether its actions stay within what it was authorised to do — across the whole transaction lifecycle. This is a foundational governance layer for agentic commerce, addressing a critical gap as autonomous agents begin making purchases on behalf of consumers.

stories.head: Contentstack Launches Canoe: AI Visibility Tool Benchmarking Brands in AI Search
stories.plain: Contentstack's first standalone product, Canoe, shows marketers exactly how AI search engines describe and cite their brand versus up to ten competitors, then outputs a ranked fix list that AI agents can execute. It is one of the first commercial tools purpose-built for Generative Engine Optimization, making it directly relevant to any brand worried about visibility in AI-driven search.

stories.head: Braze Expands AI from Content Creation to Campaign Operations
stories.plain: Braze is moving AI beyond copy generation into campaign decisioning and automated QA checks, and is opening connections to external LLMs like Claude. For buyers evaluating CEPs, this marks a shift from AI as a content helper to AI as an operational layer — changing what marketers should expect from a modern engagement platform.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Radically Different Competitive Shelves
stories.plain: Jellyfish's research shows that AI shopping assistants recommend entirely different product sets than traditional search rankings, reshuffling brand leadership and price positioning in ways most marketers haven't measured. The firm also launched a 'Share of Model™' metric to track it — giving the industry a concrete new KPI for AI shelf visibility.

themes.head: AI Search Is the New Brand Battleground
body: AI-powered search and shopping assistants are no longer a future concern — they are actively reshaping which brands get recommended and why. Jellyfish research shows that traditional brand leadership and price positioning no longer guarantee visibility when an LLM is curating answers instead of a ranked list of links.

The strategic response is emerging fast: tools like Contentstack Canoe give marketers a window into what AI actually tells buyers, while new frameworks for generative engine optimization (GEO) and visual SEO for AI search are replacing classic keyword playbooks. Brands that don't audit their AI-search presence risk disappearing from the consideration set entirely.

themes.head: Agentic AI Escapes the Sandbox
body: AI agents have moved from pilots into live go-to-market workflows — and governance hasn't kept pace. ZoomInfo's acquisition of DoubleO.ai to launch Agent Teams, Mixpanel's Agent Intelligence measurement layer, and Braze's expansion of AI into campaign operations all signal that multi-agent orchestration is becoming a default GTM architecture, not an experiment.

The accountability gap is the urgent problem: GTM teams are already losing track of what their agents are doing, and the commerce layer is reacting with trust infrastructure like Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem and DataDome's intent verification. Governing agents is now as important as deploying them.

themes.head: Speed vs. Quality: AI Made Marketing Faster, Not Better
body: A clear counter-narrative is consolidating around AI's real impact: velocity gains have outrun quality and strategic gains. Analysis of job postings shows employers scrambling for AI skills, yet practitioners are finding that faster content pipelines have not produced meaningfully better campaigns or customer outcomes.

The trust-beats-speed argument is gaining traction in practitioner commentary, and the caution extends to how teams interact with models — stopping the habit of treating LLMs like people and building disciplined prompt and evaluation practices instead. This sets up a maturity reckoning for teams that adopted AI on enthusiasm alone.

themes.head: CRM & First-Party Data Become Pipeline Engines
body: With third-party signal quality declining and AI agents needing authoritative inputs, the race is on to make CRM and first-party data directly actionable for revenue generation. Growth7's platform turning CRM data into pipeline action, Salesforce's acquisition of Listen Labs for AI-powered customer research, and CommerceIQ's retail media AI all reflect the same underlying move: proprietary data as the core competitive asset.

This shift also redraws the line between marketing and sales technology. AI is collapsing the handoff between insight, content, and outreach into a single automated loop — meaning the quality and hygiene of owned data now determines pipeline output more directly than campaign creativity does.
ev: MarTech Series · CommerceIQ retail media AI

themes.head: Regulation & AI Sovereignty Enter the Stack
body: Governance pressure is arriving from two directions at once: state legislatures rewriting social media rules and enterprises demanding self-hosted, sovereignty-compliant AI deployments. IBM's self-hosted offering for Bob is explicitly framed around AI sovereignty and governance — a vendor acknowledging that cloud-only AI is a deal-breaker for a growing share of enterprise buyers.

Simultaneously, identity fraud is becoming more AI-adaptive, pushing platforms like Persona to expand protection tooling and creating demand for verified, trustworthy data pipes across the whole stack. Compliance and trust infrastructure are graduating from legal checkbox to genuine product differentiator as regulators and enterprise risk teams close in.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — from GEO to agentic pipelines to sovereignty infrastructure — converges on a single inflection point: AI is no longer augmenting marketing decisions, it is making them, which means the teams and vendors who win will be those who govern, measure, and own their data before they scale their automation.
